headline_hook: Gemini Flash Grabs the Desktop While Lilian Weng Tears Up the Scaling Playbook
preview_topics: the AI SDK v7 migration clock

pick_of_the_day.thesis: The scaling-laws consensus that drove $100B in training compute is built on assumptions that break at the frontier — Weng's synthesis shows where the power laws bend, and why the next generation of training budgets can't just extrapolate from Chinchilla.

model_literacy.relevance: Today's scaling laws deep dive reveals that 'compute-optimal' depends on assumptions about data quality, mixture, and evaluation methodology that most scaling analyses gloss over — understanding where the framework's power laws break down matters as frontier training runs push past $1B.

items.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash Gets Computer Use — Google's Fastest Model Takes the Desktop
items.angle: Google commoditizes desktop automation at Flash-tier pricing, directly challenging Anthropic's computer use lead and making agentic UI control accessible to cost-sensitive teams
items.key_fact: Computer use now available in Gemini 3.5 Flash, Google's fastest and cheapest model tier

items.title: Vercel AI SDK Hits v7.0 With Breaking Changes You'll Feel
items.angle: Telemetry goes stable, deprecated media types get removed, and prepareStep message overrides are fixed — if you're on v6, check your imports before Monday
items.key_fact: Major version bump: experimental_ telemetry prefix dropped, deprecated ToolResultOutput media types removed

items.title: CrewAI 1.15 Goes All-In on Declarative YAML Flows
items.angle: Multi-agent pipelines defined in YAML with conditional expressions and inline crew definitions — the biggest release since CrewAI's declarative pivot
items.key_fact: YAML-defined flows now support conditional expressions, composite actions, and a conversational TUI

items.title: Ollama Auto-Installs Claude Code and OpenCode
items.angle: Ollama positions itself as the local inference layer that coding agents launch on top of — auto-install plus thinking capability detection
items.key_fact: Auto-install support for Claude Code and OpenCode, plus thinking capability detection for compatible models

items.title: Anthropic Adds Device Trust to Remote Claude Code Sessions
items.angle: Enterprise security teams get a trust boundary before anyone can view or steer a developer's local Claude Code session — remote control without device verification is now opt-out, not opt-in
items.key_fact: Device verification required before remote viewing or steering of Claude Code sessions

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.193: classifyAllShell Routes Every Bash Command Through Auto-Mode
items.angle: New setting classifies every Bash command via the auto-mode classifier, plus denial reasons in transcripts and OpenTelemetry log events for observability pipelines
items.key_fact: classifyAllShell setting applies auto-mode classification to all Bash commands, not just arbitrary-code patterns

items.title: AI SDK xAI Provider Adds Grok 4.3 and Build Model
items.angle: First SDK integration for xAI's latest model lineup including grok-build-0.1 and configurable reasoning effort
items.key_fact: Adds Grok 4.3, grok-build-0.1, grok-imagine-image-quality, plus 'none' and 'medium' reasoning effort levels

items.title: llama.cpp Gets SYCL Tensor Parallelism for Dual-GPU Inference
items.angle: Intel and AMD multi-GPU inference becomes a first-class citizen with backend-specific all-reduce mirroring the CUDA pattern
items.key_fact: --split-mode tensor now supported on SYCL backend for dual-GPU setups

items.title: Lilian Weng's Definitive Scaling Laws Guide Exposes Where the Power Laws Break
items.angle: The most comprehensive public treatment of scaling laws — covering Chinchilla, compute-optimal training, and the blind spots that could mislead billion-dollar training budget decisions
items.key_fact: Covers Chinchilla, compute-optimal training, and identifies specific regimes where power-law extrapolation fails

items.title: AllenAI Maps Where Hybrid Architectures Beat Pure Transformers Token by Token
items.angle: Practical guidance for architecture selection: hybrid attention + state-space models outperform pure transformers on specific token patterns
items.key_fact: Token-level analysis reveals which prediction patterns favor hybrid architectures over pure transformers

items.title: Un-0 Generates Images With Coupled Oscillators Instead of Diffusion
items.angle: A physics-inspired approach that sidesteps both diffusion and autoregression — opens a genuinely new design space for generative models
items.key_fact: Uses coupled oscillator dynamics for image generation, a fundamentally different approach from diffusion or autoregressive models

items.title: Trakkr Maps Political Bias Across Major AI Models
items.angle: Structured methodology for comparing model biases — useful reference for teams evaluating model choices in politically sensitive domains
items.key_fact: 213 retweets and 104 likes; structured bias comparison across major commercial models

items.title: One Command to a vLLM Server on HuggingFace Jobs
items.angle: Self-hosting open models without managing GPU clusters — HuggingFace wraps vLLM inference into a managed job you launch from the CLI
items.key_fact: Single CLI command spins up a managed vLLM inference server on HuggingFace infrastructure

items.title: Hello-Agents: From Agent Fundamentals to Production Multi-Agent Systems
items.angle: Trending tutorial that fills the gap between hello-world agent demos and real system design — walks the full path from basics to production-grade multi-agent applications
items.key_fact: 127 GitHub stars; covers fundamentals through production-grade multi-agent architecture

items.title: OpenAI Pushes IPO to 2027 — and the Valuation Ripple Hits Everyone
items.angle: The delay signals OpenAI wants more time to solidify revenue and governance, but public market comps drive private AI valuations — every AI startup's fundraise just lost a benchmark
items.key_fact: NYT reports OpenAI targeting 2027 for IPO, pushing back from earlier 2026 timeline

items.title: Simon Willison on AI Liability: Who Pays When Agents Break Things?
items.angle: As AI agents take real actions in production, liability frameworks will shape what developers can and can't ship — Willison maps the fault lines
items.key_fact: Liability analysis focused on AI agents that take real-world actions, not just generate text

items.title: Latent Space Declares 'Meta-Harness Summer'
items.angle: The orchestration-layer-on-orchestration-layer trend gets a name — useful framing for the current wave of agent-framework-of-frameworks proliferation
items.key_fact: Coins the term 'Meta-Harness Summer' for the trend of building orchestration layers atop orchestration layers

items.title: OpenKnowledge: Open-Source AI-First Alternative to Obsidian and Notion
items.angle: 175 HN points signal real demand for AI-native note-taking without vendor lock-in — Inkeep's open-source play against the incumbents
items.key_fact: 175 HN points; open-source knowledge management designed for AI-native workflows

items.title: OpenTag Routes @agent Mentions in Slack and GitHub to Codex or Claude Code
items.angle: Open-source agent routing for team workflows — @mention an agent in Slack or GitHub, get results in-thread without platform lock-in
items.key_fact: 136 GitHub stars; routes @agent mentions to Codex or Claude Code and returns results in-thread
